verdicts.verdict: All 8192 screened worlds are valid: none non-finite, none collapsed to point masses (largest cell density 48, smallest participation ratio 0.015), total mass conserved to 3.0e-14 over 290 ticks and to 1.7e-13 over 2240 ticks; the 32 no-affinity control worlds are all uniform (32). The crowding term does what the critique asked for.

The family is cheap: 74676 member-ticks/s on an H100 (85396 on an H200) in float64, so 8192 draws with full certificates took 376 s; the gliders world ran at 2035 member-ticks/s by the same code on the same pod (compile included), about 37 times slower.

World types over the prior at ticks 50-290: uniform 65.2%, frozen 19.7%, active 15.1% (field 8.0%, bodies 3.9%, movers 3.2%); no noisy and no collapsed world. Gates: closure 3.1%, structures 2.5%, sensitive 8.9%, all four 1.07% +- 0.11% (88 worlds; 1.55% without conversion, 0.57% with).

Most early activity is a transient: of the 1238 worlds active at ticks 50-290 only 37.1% are still active at ticks 2000-2240 and 61.7% have frozen; 30.2% of the movers are still movers and 32 of the 88 candidates (36.4%) still pass every gate (10 other active worlds became candidates). Frozen and uniform worlds stay as they are (4.7% and 3.7% of 381 each changed type; 1.6% of the frozen sample became active). Long-lived activity is therefore about 5.6% of the prior from early-active worlds (plus about 0.3% from early-frozen ones) and long-lived candidates about 0.51%: the screen needs a late-time gate.

Statistics of the weights alone predict the type. The growth rate of the fastest linear mode of the uniform state (two Jacobian-vector products and an FFT per world, no simulation of the field) has AUC 0.967 for structure; the rule growth > 1e-4 (36.4% of draws) has precision 0.875 and recall 0.916. Cross-validated logistic regressions on all weight statistics reach AUC 0.983 (structure), 0.920 (movers) and 0.942 (candidates); for candidates the prior's scalars alone give 0.878, linear stability 0.899, the affinity Jacobian 0.922, and the weight norms 0.511 (no information).

The predictor holds prospectively. Fitted on job 1 and applied to the weight statistics of a fresh pool of 32768 draws (another prior seed), its best 9.4% (3072 draws) contain 10.5% +- 0.6% candidates (323); predicted before the run: 9.1%. Movers 21.4% (predicted 19.3%), active 62.8% (60.0%), structured 94.0% (95.6%). The 1024 control draws, a random sample of the unselected draws, contain 0.49% (5 worlds). Weighting the two arms, the pool's candidate rate is 1.43% +- 0.20% (job 1: 1.07%); the selected draws are enriched 7.4 times and hold 69% of all candidates.

The screen's selection replicates: all 24 of the 24 top worlds pass every gate again at certification size (16 members, 32 test states, fresh keys), and 71 of all 88 candidates do (80.7%). 29 candidates pass at the screen, at certification size and at ticks 2000-2240; 7 of them have a closure profile like the gliders world's (c(1) >= 0.95, 0.25 <= c(8) <= 0.75, c(32) <= 0.5) with unchanged statistics at late time: draws 4470, 4186, 262, 7567, 6845, 1672, 3078 of prior seed 2026.

The gliders world, measured by the same code, is typed a mover world in 16 of 16 runs and passes the closure and structures gates. Its ceilings with the cheap ridge at 1/2/4/8/16/32 ticks are 0.989 / 0.959 / 0.829 / 0.480 / 0.213 / 0.031 (8 runs at certification size) against the published 0.988 / 0.955 / 0.800 / 0.371 / 0.126 / 0.007 (linear predictors) and 0.991 / 0.967 / 0.849 / 0.495 / 0.136 / 0.078 (best of all predictors); oracle variance at 8 ticks 0.0100 (published 0.0091); 7.6 bodies (published 7.4), radius 6.5 px, 1.73 px/tick, 45 fusions + fissions per 100 ticks (published 45); its plug-in loss with theta' = theta is -0.0008 +- 0.0004 (the null of that estimator). So the estimator reproduces the reference, and foundry draw 4470 sits next to it: ceilings at 1/4/8/16/32 ticks 0.991 / 0.796 / 0.480 / 0.272 / 0.193, oracle variance 0.0013, 17 bodies of radius 2.3 px at 0.45 px/tick, 62 events per 100 ticks, noise-twin doubling 2.4 ticks (gliders 1.8).

The hidden weights matter for prediction. On the 24 certified worlds, predicting 8 ticks ahead with a neighbour's weights costs (median) 0.0074, 0.078 and 0.39 of the climatological variance for weight neighbours at 3%, 10% and 30%, and 0.160 when the scalars move by 10% of their prior range as well, against an oracle variance of 0.0020: 5 and 45 times the oracle's own error at 3% and 10% (all 88 candidates at 10%: 29 times).

The type belongs to the weights, not to the public noise level: of 2048 draws, 99.4% keep their type (uniform / frozen / active) when the logit noise goes from 0.3 to 0.1 and 93.4% when it goes to 1.0 (there 73 of 414 frozen worlds become active fields); 70 and 64 of 73 movers stay movers; candidates 24 -> 25 and 29.

The wind channel is exact but weak. Its charge is exact by construction and checks numerically (12.48 +- 0.08 nats by Monte Carlo against 12.37 charged); a unit command on every block (512 nats per tick) moves passive matter by 0.25 and 0.36 px per tick. But on four top worlds (draws 1672, 4470, 262, 60) a 4-tick command of 200 nats aimed at the densest block changes the block view by only 0.0002 to 0.023 of its variance 4 ticks later (1.6 to 7.9 times the noise floor), and a blind command of 200 nats stays below the floor (0.09 to 0.28 times). 'Actions matter' is not established for these worlds; the channel needs a redesign and its own certificate.

Exploration only (CPU, the same four worlds, draws 1672, 4470, 262, 60): with the wind noise at 1.0 instead of 0.25 (a given force is 16 times cheaper in nats) the aimed 200-nat command changes the block view by 0.233, 0.095, 0.002, 0.088 of its variance at 4 ticks (before: 0.0228, 0.0027, 0.0002, 0.0058), but the wind's own noise then raises the noise floor at 4 ticks about 11 times (median); the types under that background wind were not re-measured.

Platform: float64. On the H100 a rerun of the same compiled batch is bit-identical (True) and vmap equals single-world runs exactly; the four certification runs of job 1 returned identical main-run numbers. The screen of 12 draws repeated on this container's CPU with the same keys gives the same type 12 of 12 times; for 8 non-chaotic draws all 608 of 608 stored values are identical, for 4 movers they differ by at most 0.8%. Unlike the gliders world (FFT, scatter), this law is built from elementwise operations and shifts only.

CPU runs of 2000 ticks of draws 1672, 4470, 262, 60: net body speed 0.61, 0.56, 0.83, 0.33 px/tick in the first 250 ticks and 0.61, 0.53, 0.65, 0.38 in the last 250; bodies 4.1, 19.3, 12.1, 5.1 and 3.4, 19.7, 10.9, 4.4.

decides: A random weights-as-law family is viable and cheap: a 10^5-draw screen with certificates is about 77 minutes of one H100 (about $6.4 at $5.02/h), not the 20-80 GPU-hours DESIGN.md E2 budgeted.

DESIGN.md E2's rule (gate pass rate >= 10%: random families suffice; <= 1%: invest in search): the pass rate is about 1% early and about 0.5% once transients are excluded, so plain random draws do not suffice, but no search is needed either: the weights-only predictor concentrates 69% of the candidates in 9.4% of the draws at no simulation cost, and screening is cheap enough to brute-force the rest.
Every screen must carry a late-time gate (a 2000-tick burn-in costs 4.6 times the short screen per draw; applied to the 15% early-active draws only it adds about 69%).

Seven foundry worlds are ready to be certified as exam candidates next to the gliders world (same closure band at level 1, moving and interacting bodies, stationary, strongly weight-sensitive); what they lack is an input channel that matters.
Publishing the weights-only predictor is safe only with the published criteria: selection narrows the posterior on theta (DESIGN.md section 5); here it is a public function of theta by construction.
never_reuse_as_exam: Prior seeds 1, 2026 and 2027 with run seed 5150 are pilots: their weights are a public function of (seed, index) and hidden parameters of several draws are printed in these results. They must never be reused as exam instances; an exam draws theta from a secret seed.
